About the Role

Industrious signs new landlord partnerships every year, and the number is growing as our business development team expands. Before any of those deals move forward, someone has to check that it holds together: that the assumptions are sound, that the start date, budgets, rent, pricing, and returns all track, and that the figures from design and construction have carried through correctly. As a Real Estate Associate on our Real Estate Transactions team that will be your job!

You will underwrite assigned deals in Excel, explain what drives their returns, and flag where a deal is tight, whether on pricing, occupancy, or CapEx. Our business development colleagues make the call on whether a deal goes ahead, and your analysis is what they rely on to make it well. You will work with Design, Construction, Finance, and other teams to make sure every number is right, supporting several business development colleagues as deal flow shifts.

Our approach to underwriting is different from a traditional real estate shop, and we will teach it to you. In your first few months you will get close review and clear guidance while you learn how we work. You will also join at a good time: the team is growing, new roles are being added, and we are underwriting a new product, so there is real room to learn, ask questions, and grow with us.

Success here means accurate work. The team trusts your numbers, your flags are clear, and any mistake you make happens once, not twice.

What Might Your Day Look Like

Your morning starts with a new deal from one of our business development colleagues. You go through the model piece by piece: the start date, the budget, the rent and revenue share assumptions, the cash flows, the IRR, and the margin the location is expected to earn per rentable square foot. The returns look fine at first, but pricing is tighter than it seems, so you note it clearly with the number that would need to change.

Late morning, updated figures arrive from Design and Construction. You check that they have flowed into the model correctly. One CapEx figure does not match the construction budget, so you confirm the right number with the construction team before it goes any further.

In the afternoon, you walk your business development colleague through the deal: what the returns look like, where the risk sits, and which assumptions matter most. They decide what happens next. Then priorities shift, and another colleague needs support on a deal heading to Investment Committee, so you move over and check that every figure in the review material ties back to the underwriting.

Before you wrap up, you update your trackers and checklists so the team knows where every deal you are supporting stands.

- Underwrite assigned deals in Excel

Construction is a $2 trillion industry in the US alone. Most of it still runs like it’s 1995: PDFs, spreadsheets, and email.

Every commercial building starts the same way. Someone opens a few hundred pages of blueprints and counts every piece of equipment, duct, and pipe by hand. Then they price it, bid it, and chase it for months. That work decides who builds what, and for how much. It has barely changed in 30 years.

Rebar is building the AI platform the trades run on. Our models read blueprints the way a veteran in the trades does. Our agents then do the work that follows: counting the job, pricing it, managing the bid, and tracking it through to the order. Counts that took three days now take one. Customers spend hours a day in Rebar, and thousands of new plan sets flow through it every week.

We started with HVAC contractors and their suppliers. Every other trade comes next.

We are seeking to fill the role of Assumption Loan Processor. The ideal candidate enjoys collaborating with clients, industry partners and internal teams to maximize outcomes for homeowners.
Responsibilities

• Review loan documents to determine if loan is assumable.

• Prepare and distribute approval and denial letters.

• Prepare and distribute assumption packages.

• Receive assumption packages and log according to department procedures.

• Inspect file documents to ensure completeness and contact borrowers/applicants to obtain missing documents.

• Obtain relevant documents from applicant(s) and submit request for mortgage insurance approval.

• Upload loan documents to vendor website.

• Upload and report documents from completed assumptions to government agencies (FHA, VA, USDA, etc.).

• Make system changes to reflect new borrower (s) MERs and generate SNOW tickets.

• Pull CAIVRS and OFAC reports.

• Pull credit reports, and prepare Verifications of Employment and Verifications of Mortgage.

• Review Trusts & LLCs to ensure they meet agency guidelines.

• Follow procedures to ensure compliance with internal business standards and applicable federal, state, local or other regulatory disclosures and requirements.

• Provide support as needed with audits and to department members.

• Act as a liaison between various functional areas and customers to reach conclusions with customers.

• All other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

• High School Diploma or equivalent required.

• 2+ years mortgage experience.

• General knowledge of overall mortgage lending processes, documents and terminology.

• Knowledge and understanding of financial products and services.

• Knowledge of FHA, VA, Conventional and USDA loans. Ability to navigate multiple computer systems, applications and utilize tools to find information.

Desired Skills and Qualifications

• Associate’s degree in business or related field.

• Prior work experience in consumer relations/customer service positions requiring excellent verbal and written communication skills is preferred.

• Prior experience processing assumptions.
